extraction.name: CoNLL-2003 Shared Task: Language-Independent Named Entity Recognition
extraction.description: The CoNLL-2003 shared task focused on language-independent named entity recognition, involving the development of systems for identifying named entities (persons, organizations, locations, and miscellaneous entities) in English and German text. The task included training, development, and test datasets, with participants using machine learning techniques and external resources like gazetteers and unannotated data to improve system performance.
extraction.creator: Erik F. Tjong Kim Sang and Fien De Meulder
extraction.publisher: CNTS - Language Technology Group, University of Antwerp
extraction.citeAs: Erik F. Tjong Kim Sang and Fien De Meulder. Introduction to the CoNLL-2003 Shared Task: Language-Independent Named Entity Recognition. In Proceedings of CoNLL-2003, 2003.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The CoNLL-2003 named entity data consists of eight files covering two languages: English and German. For each language, there is a training file, a development file, a test file, and a large file with unannotated data. The English data was taken from the Reuters Corpus (news stories between August 1996 and August 1997), while the German data was extracted from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus (Frankfurter Rundschau newspaper articles from late August 1992).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: English data: Reuters Corpus (news stories). German data: ECI Multilingual Text Corpus (Frankfurter Rundschau newspaper articles).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: English: August 1996 to August 1997 (training/development: late August 1996; test: December 1996; raw data: September 1996). German: Late August 1992 (all datasets).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Participants were given access to the corpus after linguistic preprocessing: tokenization, part-of-speech tagging, and chunking. English data was tagged and chunked using the MBT tagger, while German data was lemmatized, tagged, and chunked using the Treetagger. Named entity tagging was done manually at the University of Antwerp following MUC conventions with an added MISC category.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Named entity tagging was performed manually at the University of Antwerp, following MUC conventions with an additional MISC category for entities not fitting the other categories. The IOB tagging scheme was used to annotate named entities (persons, organizations, locations, and miscellaneous).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Manual annotation by human annotators at the University of Antwerp
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The IOB tagging scheme was used, with tags indicating whether a word is inside a named entity (I-XXX) or outside (O). Embedded entities were annotated at the top level only.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to news articles from specific timeframes and sources (Reuters for English, Frankfurter Rundschau for German), which may not represent broader linguistic or cultural contexts. The MISC category is highly diverse, including adjectives and events, which may introduce ambiguity.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation for Named Entity Recognition (NER) systems in English and German. The dataset was designed for shared task competitions to evaluate and compare NER systems.
